rationale: The cranberry-drink trial gives inconclusive HADS depression and depression-dejection contrasts. The COMBAT cranberry-powder protocol scheduled PHQ-9, but the full publication and supplement give no depression comparison. Both cohorts were outside Parkinson disease. The dried-cranberry hypothesis remains unresolved.

Parkinson interview reports and controlled whole-rhizome comparisons supply a minimal favorable lean. Separate extract trials report favorable perineal and abdominal pain findings, inconclusive uterine and joint-pain outcomes, and exercise or menstrual reporting discrepancies. Differences in preparation, condition, comparison, and reporting limit transfer to grated ginger and Parkinson pain.

An unblinded non-Parkinson trial reports a favorable turmeric powder and naproxen comparison, with unresolved enrollment and design differences versus its registry. A hand-osteoarthritis pilot gives an inconclusive primary pain comparison and favorable three-month within-arm changes. Isolated curcumin animal results use different exposures and pain proxies. The unblinded whole-powder comparison supplies a minimal favorable lean, with Parkinson pain unresolved.
